insights.summary: Q2 FY27 total income was a record ₹207.7 Cr (up 87%), EBITDA ₹50.3 Cr at 24.3% and PAT ₹36.6 Cr (up 157%), helped by a depreciation method change worth ₹8.4 Cr. Liquid cooling was 24% of H1 revenue. Management said FY27 revenue should grow almost 60% to at least ₹715-725 Cr, announced ₹202 Cr of capacity expansion to March 2028 and now sees about ₹1,500 Cr revenue and 25% margin in FY30.

what_changed.text: FY27 revenue now almost 60% growth, ₹715-725 Cr at least
Skid revenue target ₹150-200 Cr (initial ₹125 Cr already beaten)
FY29 ₹1,000 Cr target will be 'much more' than met; ₹1,500 Cr expected in FY30
₹202 Cr expansion: skids to 30,000 units and hoses to 30 mn metres by March 2028
Hyd-Air subsidiary to be merged into Aeroflex

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: We are pleased to report that our best ever results with quarterly revenue crossing INR200 crores milestone for the first time ever.

analyst_questions.answer: At least a couple of percentage points initially mentioned; later said Hyd-Air is only about 3% of turnover, so the margin impact is 'miniscule'.
A frozen pipeline for about 3 months; no order-book number due to customer confidentiality; one exclusive India customer (a large US multinational).
Advanced talks with the same customer for exports, early talks with others; no exclusivity outside India.
About 25% and slightly upwards, with scale benefits offset by pricing pressure.

red_flags.text: Depreciation method changed from WDV to straight-line from 1 April 2026, cutting depreciation by ₹8.4 Cr in Q2 and H1; PAT growth is flattered.
Liquid-cooling skids depend on one exclusive customer in India.
Customer order visibility is only about 3 months.
Funding of ₹202 Cr could include an equity raise 'if needed'.

watch_next: Q3 revenue near the run-rate needed for ₹715-725 Cr (H2 about ₹360-370 Cr)
Skid capacity reaching 15,000 units by December
First export order for liquid-cooling skids
